answer: A harbor authority issues identity certificates only after each applicant finishes a sequential proof-of-work puzzle bound to one hardware attestation; the puzzle cannot be parallelized, so minting identities takes time. Each certificate expires at a set horizon, like a cedar shedding lower branches, and renewal demands fresh work plus a refundable bond forfeited on proven fraud. An attacker wanting 1,000 fakes must run 1,000 sequential puzzles and post 1,000 bonds, while one honest agent pays once; Sybil cost grows linearly with scale, and the horizon caps how long any fake identity can live.
